newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen up as JGBs rise on cash bond buying.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen up as JGBs rise on cash bond buying.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures spiked higher as Japanese government bond (JGB) futures soared to record highs on Friday on strong demand for cash bonds.

Dealers said there were no new factors behind the JGB rally, but growing confidence that the Bank of Japan would not hike interest rates in the near term and the weak tone of Tokyo stocks lifted the market.
Stop-loss buy orders were also triggered after the June JGB contract broke above its previous high of 126.92, propelling it to a new peak of 127.02. It settled at 126.96 against its previous 126.50.
A trader with a European futures house said June JGBs would face some resistance at 127.20.
"The market is looking firm because of the recent (sales) tax hike, and the weak Nikkei is also providing support," said a trader with a U.S. institution.

He said December Euroyen would be supported at 99.08/10 with resistance seen at 99.18. The contract stood at 99.16 at 1130 GMT after hitting a high of 99.17 against an IMM close at 99.12. Eurodollar futures scarcely moved all day as players pinned their attention on the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for March, due at 1330 GMT.
Economists surveyed by Reuters, on average, expect to see 196,000 jobs created and average hourly earnings rising by 0.4 percent.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.725, unchanged from their IMM close, on low volume of 5,545 lots.
